title: Resolve SSE fragment reassembly and out-of-order event framing for OpenAI compatibility
author: Lina Moreno
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming bug where partial JSON events could be mis-framed across network chunk boundaries causing client-side JSON parse errors; improved reassembly and ordering guarantees in the OpenAI compatibility SSE layer. Backwards-compatible: adds optional event_sequence header for robust client reordering.
description:
Context and motivation: Several production customers reported spurious parsing errors when consuming streaming responses from our OpenAI-compatible SSE endpoint. Symptoms included JSON decode errors from partial object chunks, occasional scrambled tool/function_call payloads, and clients observing events out-of-order when network proxies split frames. Reproduction: 1) Simulate small MTU/slow connections that split SSE 'data:' payloads mid-JSON (e.g. '{"choices": [ {"delta": {"content": "hel' then 'lo"}} ] }'). 2) Proxy that injects an extra '
' delimiter between frames or merges small writes into a single TCP segment. Root cause: Our existing SSE chunking logic assumed that each 'data:' event contained a complete JSON payload or a single text delta. When the upstream runtime emitted partial token/text chunks, the OpenAI-compat layer attempted to decode the chunk immediately. Two related problems surfaced:  - Delimiter normalization bug: the handler sometimes emitted extra empty 'data:' lines (double newlines) which downstream clients treated as separators and attempted to parse an empty payload.  - Reassembly and ordering: without a lightweight sequence or stable buffer, clients could see function_call events interleaved with token-delta events if proxies re-ordered or coalesced writes. What I changed: 1) Robust chunk parser (openai_compat/sse/parser.py): Implemented a streaming JSON reassembly buffer that:   - Buffers partial 'data:' payloads until a valid JSON object can be parsed or until an explicit '[DONE]' sentinel is received.   - Uses a conservative brace/bracket balance scan first, then attempts a streaming json.loads() only when balance indicates a candidate complete object to avoid expensive trial parses on every fragment.   - Normalizes newline/delimiter sequences so we never emit empty 'data:' events. 2) Event sequencing (openai_compat/sse/handler.py):   - Added an optional per-event sequence counter (event_sequence) emitted as a header on each SSE event for internal compatibility clients. This is opt-in and defaults to off for strict OpenAI parity, but is enabled in our hosted deployments for safety.   - The handler will now preserve original upstream ordering and attach sequence metadata when reassembly spans multiple upstream writes. 3) Function-calls and structured output stability:   - Ensure function_call start/complete deltas are coalesced into a single function_call JSON payload before emitting to clients. 4) Tests and examples:   - Added integration test that simulates interleaved TCP/write fragmentation and proxy-induced delimiter insertion. 5) Observability:   - Expose a reassembly_latency histogram and a drop/retry counter so we can track regressions. Backwards compatibility and safety notes: - Clients that rely on strict OpenAI SSE formatting will see no semantic change to event shapes. The event_sequence header is optional and for robustness; we document it in the compatibility docs. - The parser is defensive and will time out/emit an error event if reassembly exceeds a configurable byte/time threshold. Commit summary: - 8b2f1c9: sse: add streaming brace-balance reassembler and delimiter normalizer - d4a7e12: sse: attach event_sequence and preserve upstream ordering when configured - c7f3b40: tests: simulate fragmented writes and proxy delimiter injection - 1a9e4d5: docs: add section on event_sequence and recommended client behavior - 9f0b2a1: examples: streaming_fragments.js client showing tolerant reassembly Failure modes considered: - Extremely pathological fragmentation (single-byte writes) will increase CPU work on parse attempts; mitigated with cheap balance-scan and configurable thresholds. - Clients that blindly parse every 'data:' event will still see transient errors; recommending clients adopt the documented reassembly behavior. How to validate locally: - Run tests: pytest openai_compat/tests/test_sse_reassembly.py - Run the example node client: node examples/openai/streaming_fragments.js and confirm it receives 3 complete JSON messages and one [DONE]. Related: ENG-3124 (customer incident), infra/mtu-proxy tickets. Checklists: - [x] Add parser and handler changes - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add docs and example client - [x] CI green + e2e passes - [x] Merge to main and bump changelog Links: - Design doc (internal): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3124/sse-reassembly-design - Example reproduction harness commit: changes included in this PR
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Nice catch — can you add a knob to disable event_sequence in case customers want exact OpenAI header parity?
Lina Moreno: Added config flag 'OPENAI_COMPAT_EVENT_SEQUENCE=false' in handler and documented it. Also kept default enabled in hosted envs.
Devon Liu: Can we avoid a second json.loads() pass when reassembling large objects? Benchmark the balance-scan approach.
Lina Moreno: Benchmarks added to parser module; balance-scan avoids repeated loads in >98% of fragments. Added microbenchmark to tests.
Marcus Reyes: Tests look good. One nit: increase the reassembly timeout to 2s in envs with high latency proxies.
Lina Moreno: Increased timeout and made it configurable via REDWOOD_SSE_REASSEMBLY_TIMEOUT_MS.

changelog_entry: Fixed: SSE framing and partial JSON reassembly bug in OpenAI compatibility layer. Improved robustness to fragmented TCP writes and proxy delimiter injection (ENG-3124).
